Noah (Dir Platform): Quick thread to align on 'residency-first lanes' — customers want hard guarantees for where inference executes. We need a product/infra roadmap, clear launch gates, and a conservative rollout plan.

Hannah (Product): From GTM: enterprise customers ask for a toggle that enforces regional residency + an SLA. They also expect a migration path for existing reserved capacity customers.

Jae (Backend): Architecturally we can do policy lanes: residency-enforced vs best-effort affinity. Residency-enforced = route only to nodes with matching region tag and reserved capacity check. This requires routing-side capacity checks and a per-tenant sticky assignment store.

Priya (SRE): Ops concerns: if a region loses capacity, enforced residency means traffic will queue or fail — we must define an eviction policy (evict to backup region only with explicit customer consent) and automated alerts.

Noah (Dir Platform): Let's define phases: alpha internal + infra tests, private pilot (opt-in customers), limited GA (enterprise only), full GA (self-serve). Each phase has gating metrics.

Hannah (Product): Suggested customer-facing commitments per phase: Pilot = "regional residency where possible; fallbacks documented"; GA = "regional residency guaranteed when reserved capacity contract present; SLA: availability 99.9% for regional-serving". Need pricing update for guaranteed lane.

Jae (Backend): Implementation notes:
- Routing: add policy evaluation step before placement.
- Placement: node-tag match and capacity token check.
- Cache: per-region KV cache shard; warmers to prefill model caches when a tenant pins region.
- Control plane: per-tenant policy object + history.

Priya (SRE): Gating metrics draft:
- Regional-p95 token latency within 1.5x baseline for pinned tenants across 7d
- Routing-induced 5xx < 0.1% over 24h for pilot tenants
- Startup cold-start errors during switchover < 0.5%
- Eviction events count per week < 2 for pilot cohort
- Telemetry completeness: region tags + placement traces present for 99% of calls

Noah (Dir Platform): Rollback/kill switches: per-tenant feature flag, global kill switch for residency enforcement, and automatic circuit that flips to affinity lane if route latency exceeds threshold for > 30s. Who owns these?

Priya (SRE): SRE owns the global kill switch + playbooks. Platform team owns per-tenant flags and rollout orchestration. Engineers own runtime changes. We'll add runbook sections: detection, mitigation, manual eviction steps.

Hannah (Product): Pilot cohort criteria: small-to-medium customers (5-40 rps), no compliance restrictions, footprint in target region, willing to run with opt-in billing model. Also require a signed pilot MOU describing fallback behavior.

Jae (Backend): Data consistency note: we can't do cross-region strong KV sync. Plan: authoritative placement in control plane (single writer per region for placements), async replication for read-only caches. Accept eventual consistency for placement metadata with TTL and versioned placement tokens.

Noah (Dir Platform): Cost modeling: we need an estimate of egress + reserved idle capacity overhead. Jae, can you produce a simple cost simulator (30min prototype) that projects per-tenant delta?

Jae (Backend): Yes — I'll push a small script to the infra repo: `tools/cost_probe/residency_sim.py`. It will simulate trafficsplits, egress, and idle-reservation overhead.

Priya (SRE): Canary plan: roll residency enforcement into canary cluster with synthetic tenants that exercise hot cache, cold-starts, and burst traffic. Use traffic shaping to keep blast radius minimal. Deploy-bot can kick off canary.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy started -> cluster: residency-canary-01, manifest: residency-v0.1

Hannah (Product): Comms: Pilot invite should include expected behavior matrix, support contacts, and metrics we'll monitor (latency, placement fidelity, eviction events). Also clarify rollback terms for customers.

Noah (Dir Platform): Decision points for GA: telemetry shows stable latency (gating metrics met for 14d), eviction events <= threshold, cost delta acceptable (<15%). If any one fails, keep in opt-in.

Jae (Backend): Policy precedence sketch (pseudo):
```
if tenant.policy.enforce_residency:
  if region.has_reserved_capacity(tenant): route_to_reserved_region
  elif tenant.allows_fallback: route_to_affinity_lane
  else: return error(RESIDENCY_NOT_AVAILABLE)
else if tenant.policy.prefer_region:
  prefer local_region else fallback_to_cheapest
else:
  global_default_routing()
```

Priya (SRE): Alerting thresholds: create alerts for high placement qps, long queue lengths in pinned nodes (>500ms request queue), and placement mismatch rate. Tie to oncall paging.

Hannah (Product): Action items:
- Jae: prototype cost simulator + initial runtime PR for policy evaluation (due Fri)
- Priya: draft canary runbook and alert rules (due Mon)
- Noah: pilot invite + pilot MOU template (due Fri)
- Hannah: pricing notes + SLA language for pilot (due Fri)

Noah (Dir Platform): We'll reconvene next Thursday 10:00 PT to review canary results. If blockers, post on this thread. Thanks. :raised_hands:

deploy-bot: cluster residency-canary-01 health: OK (router, placer, telemetry)

Jae (Backend): pushed branch `residency/policy-eval` -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/placer/pull/88 (WIP)

Priya (SRE): created grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/residency/overview (shared with pilot cohort)

Hannah (Product): draft MOU in drive: https://redwood.app/drive/pilot-mou-residency-v1

Noah (Dir Platform): Nice progress. If anyone adds significant design changes, drop a short summary here so product and SRE can re-evaluate gating metrics.
